title: Deliver one feature
summary: Takes one feature from its written spec to a signed, scanned, verified and security-reviewed build.

start.github: /sdd status F## (comment on the phase pull request)

steps.title: Clarify the spec
steps.does: Bob looks for gaps and asks up to eight questions; the analyst answers; answers are recorded in spec.md.

steps.title: Plan the build
steps.does: Bob drafts plan.md against the constitution checklist; contract, ADR and design changes are allowed while the plan is unapproved.

steps.title: Owner signs the plan
steps.does: The signature is bound to the hashes of plan.md and spec.md: the spec is locked from here on, and any change goes through the change-request workflow.

steps.title: Split into tasks
steps.does: Bob breaks the signed plan into small test-first tasks, each tagged with the requirements it serves.

steps.title: Build, test first
steps.subagents: Independent task groups may run as parallel subagents; each commit still names its task and requirement IDs.
steps.does: One commit per task: failing tagged test, code, tests green, tick the task. On GitHub, a developer can ask Bob to address review findings on the pull request.

steps.title: Security scan
steps.does: The security checks in sdd/governance/checks.json (or SonarQube, if it is the scanner) give the verdict; it is bound to a fingerprint of the code it saw. Any later code change makes it stale.

steps.title: Prove every example
steps.does: Every acceptance criterion gets a tagged test; the verification report and traceability matrix are written.

steps.title: Security review
steps.does: An ASVS L2 review of what tools cannot see: authorization, business logic and the domain invariants, secrets, audit.

github.pullRequest: One draft pull request per phase into main. Plans and the phase are signed by comments on it.
